title: Follow the money.
caption: LedgerLens · Guided Figma prototype walkthrough
text: LedgerLens helps a small business find where money is slipping away, inspect the evidence, and prepare a fix. This walkthrough shows the reconstructed Figma prototype. The full working application and its source code are linked in the submission deck.

title: Four findings. One clear opportunity.
caption: $1,058 one-time + $3,228 recurring annually
text: The demo company is Acme Outdoor. It is fictional. LedgerLens's existing finance engine identifies four opportunities from eleven hundred and eighty-seven bank and sales records: a duplicate payment, margin erosion, underpricing, and a subscription increase. Together, they represent four thousand, two hundred and eighty-six dollars in first-year opportunity. This is identified value, not money already recovered.

title: One invoice. Paid twice.
caption: September 2 + September 7 · Invoice INV-20418
text: Follow the duplicate-payment finding. The evidence view brings the two source records together. Both payments are for one thousand and fifty-eight dollars. They share invoice I N V, two zero four one eight, and are five days apart. The point is to make a claim inspectable. The owner can compare the amount, the invoice reference, and the dates before taking the next step.

title: A fix, ready for your judgment.
caption: Prepared request · Not sent
text: Next, LedgerLens prepares a refund request using that evidence. The draft states what happened and asks the supplier to confirm a duplicate payment. The owner stays in control. In this focused prototype, approval only records a local demo decision. It does not send an email or move money.

title: A decision you can trace.
caption: $1,058 identified · $0 recovered
text: The review state records who decided, which invoice supports the decision, and what was actually executed. It clearly separates identified opportunity from recovered cash. From here, the viewer can reset the prototype, open the full LedgerLens product, or inspect the public source repository.

title: A workflow with a traceable handoff.
caption: Existing code → Figma Design → exported tokens → working code
text: The team had used Figma earlier, but those files were lost. This session reconstructed and refined the workflow from the existing build. A Figma agent created four native, linked Design states, semantic variables, and a reusable button. The actual variables were exported back into the runnable prototype's C S S. The tree artwork and financial figures also come from the existing code.

title: Show the friction. Keep the evidence.
caption: Four stages · Tool choices · Time estimates · Ratings · Outputs
text: Screenshot review caught clipped evidence cards and wrapped labels, which were corrected. Checks covered the totals, the approval gate, repeated approval, and reset. A Figma Make upload was blocked by the environment, so we retained the native prototype and packaged runnable source. The stage log records these limits honestly. LedgerLens: find the leak, show the proof, and keep the owner in control.
